observations.finding: E-qOUT improvements include foreign patches covering the marked weak reference while yellow q lies outside the patch. Pooled predicts D; ordered crosses raw0 to E. Remaining wood, slots, steel and floor remain visible in the crop.
observations.limit: These are conditional recorded-cue labels, not evidence the entire crop is occluded or that q is an owned target pixel.

observations.finding: SHAM-D-qIN regressions retain the cyan weak reference/region while a same donor patch is displaced onto the yellow q. Ordered predicts E although pooled retained D. The matched COVER/SHAM changes position rather than donor appearance.
observations.limit: Shows an observable D-retention tradeoff, not proof that a specific token or q pixel caused the decision.

observations.finding: Both-wrong E examples visibly contain orange foreign patches but both models predict D; substantial original structural appearance remains around the patch.
observations.limit: Visible foreign material alone does not establish the expected cue relation. The weak r association and uncertainty remain source-conditional.

observations.finding: Both-wrong SHAM examples have large cones near/on q while the protected reference remains outside them; both outputs are E.
observations.limit: Consistent with failure to separate foreign-object presence from weak expected-cue visibility in these examples; not a causal feature-usage demonstration.

observations.finding: Some SHAM cases improve in the ordered arm, including a TOMIE example. The effect is not a universal shift toward E.
observations.limit: First distinct-cue occurrence rule determines examples; few original frames and correlated donors/jitters cannot estimate broad transfer accuracy.

limitations: VAL selection is original public source development VAL, not private/current/V112 or a fresh blind holdout. TRAIN is excluded from displayed cases and counted separately.
The first4 distinct-cue rule selected mostly the earliest LOCO cue indices:24 diagnostic cases span only5 distinct cues and3 source groups. It is not a material-balanced representative sample.
C19 compares two complete trained arms with matched parameter budget; ordered nodes versus pooled-repeat changes spatial information/aggregation, not pure ordering alone.

Raw panels preserve original RGB96 pixels; markers are separate display-only copies. q/r use exact crop inverse. Region original endpoint conventions remain in manifest; displayed rectangles do not redefine alpha or GT.
No weak label, uncertainty, q/L, fold, threshold, model or promotion rule changed. No training design is inferred from current/private examples.
